description: Role -> tier -> worker. The rules (rules/) speak only of tiers and roles; the concrete model, effort and per-host role priorities are set in the workers list here. Model API support, app modes, launcher policy and measured results are kept distinct. Codex delegates cannot use ultra.
precedence: model-bindings.local.json overrides keys at the same path (dictionaries merge key by key; arrays and scalars are replaced whole; workers_local merges rows by id). harness-route.py selects a worker from the workers list, the role, the host and the declared budget, and the launcher uses that resolved value. Nothing queries usage or servers at start-up. Runtime boundary: docs/runtime-boundary.md.

catalog.note: In-process agents pin effort in frontmatter; claude-run.sh passes --effort explicitly. Opus 5.5 API default effort is medium; never rely on the default.

openai.effort_note: The Astra API lists low/medium/high/xhigh/max explicitly (model page re-read 2026-10-06; API default medium per the latest-model guide). The Codex models page (2026-10-06) says "Start with Light for Astra", "Start with High for Luna" and, for GPT-6.1 Sol, the client default; The same page states: Light in the desktop app, ChatGPT Work on the web and the IDE extension, or Low in the CLI, suits quick, well-scoped tasks, so Light = model_reasoning_effort=low (verified 2026-10-06). The installed CLI cache (~/.codex/models_cache.json, fetched 2026-10-06) lists low/medium/high/xhigh/max/ultra for Astra with default_reasoning_level medium and multi_agent_reasoning_effort xhigh; GPT-6.1 Sol has default_reasoning_level low, so the client default the page refers to is low on this CLI. The S lane runs at medium (user decision 2026-10-19); high/xhigh/max rows are conditional and need an explicit --worker. Codex app Ultra is an automatic sub-agent mode; the delegation launcher and router refuse it under the no-redelegation contract. max is -b only. The enumeration in the official config-reference is separate and does not replace a measured success on the installed CLI. The human main session's model and mode are never changed.

probe.command: codex exec -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort=<effort> -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check "Reply with exactly: OK" < /dev/null

probe.note: A catalog or leaderboard listing is not runnability. A candidate enters alternatives/pending_replacement only with a probe result and date; it becomes a worker row only after a successful probe on the installed CLI and account.
probe.stdin_note: codex-cli 0.159.x reads additional input from stdin when it is not closed; a manual probe without '< /dev/null' waits instead of answering. The launchers already pass the prompt on stdin.

properties: data never leaves the LAN (which does not mean the same machine — security-boundary.md)
local.note: Model, hardware and endpoint live in model-bindings.local.json. vendors.local.endpoint requires base_url and model; wire, max_tokens and max_input_chars are optional. The request timeout is local-run.sh -t seconds (default 300, max 570). Requests happen only through local-run.sh; SessionStart never queries the server. Input format, access limits and failure handling: docs/runtime-boundary.md. Addresses, model names and measured figures stay in local settings only.

orchestrate.switch: User-selected main model stays selected; no automatic host/model switch.
orchestrate.note: The host the human started is the orchestrator. Bindings are recommended tiers and never change an already chosen main model automatically.

second_opinion.when: Consequential uncertainty unresolved by task checks, or project/user-required advice; not every planning folder.
second_opinion.vendor: different from actual design author(s); defaults to host author unless --author-vendor supplied
second_opinion.note: max is -b + --wait only. Codex delegate ultra is refused because it redelegates automatically. Model and app support evidence follows vendors.openai.guidance_sources.
second_opinion.effort_rule: Use the selected host/role binding and launcher-supported effort; no common vendor-independent effort floor.

implement.escalate_when: one step, only when a reasoning shortfall is diagnosed

write.tier_rule: decided by audience and open decisions
write.vendor_rule: decided by writing specialty (specialties); fields without a specialty use the tier default

review.tier_rule: the risk tier is the floor
review.tier1_route: Affected checks + diff; when independent review is needed, review_gate with actual target authors (--author-vendor) selects a different vendor.
review.tier2_route: review_deep (B+) with actual implementer authors; optional separate spec gate uses designer authors. Required pairs must also use different reviewer vendors.
review.tier2_inline_rule: Supply focused inline context or an exact bounded readable file/range. If access is unavailable inline the target or report incomplete; never review unseen material.
review.tier2_vendor_precedence_exception: Choose a vendor different from the author. The reviewer is not pinned to the orchestrating vendor, and when two reviews are required the reviewers must differ from each other too.
review.round_limit_note: Normally one round; second only for a blocker. Confirmation counts; no recurring whole-repo review.
review.author_tier_note: harness-route.py --author-tier <band> derives the review floor from the actual author's band: the same band on a different vendor for plan_review, review_gate and review_deep (user decision 2026-10-19). An explicit --tier overrides it; the role band_floor still applies as a minimum. When no foreground row meets a derived band (A-band OpenAI = Sol max), the router returns the detached row with needs_detached rather than a lower band.

plan_review.author_tier: same band as the design author (review.author_tier_rule)

review_gate.author_tier: same band as the implementation author (review.author_tier_rule)

review_deep.author_tier: same band as the implementation author (review.author_tier_rule)

vendor_precedence.rationale: Review by a vendor other than the author is the rule; design and implementation stay on one vendor by default (implementation_default = same, user decision 2026-10-20), so the other vendor is the review lane and the clearly separated area to switch to when one side runs out of quota. harness-route.py --vendor <other vendor> crosses implementation on purpose; a declared-exhausted default vendor hands the route to another vendor automatically. The route is re-selected from the actual authoring vendor, risk and availability.
vendor_precedence.overridden_by: specialties and hard constraints (vision, web, isolation, platform, data that must not leave) beat this order. Never the other way round.
vendor_precedence.note: by_orchestrator orders cross-vendor candidates (write/decide, and implementation when --vendor names another vendor or the default vendor is exhausted); with implementation_default = same the implementation lane is the host's own vendor. The HTML specialty is kept.
vendor_precedence.implementation_vendor: same: the design author's vendor (host vendor, or the previous worker's vendor on a retry); the route reports same_vendor: true, separation_satisfied: false. --vendor <other> crosses; reviews never accept --vendor. Set implementation_default to "other" to restore cross-vendor implementation as the default.

budget.rationale: The user's declaration feeds route selection. No automatic usage lookup and no main-model switching.

values.normal: No additional declared budget limit. Does not guarantee the account's actual remaining usage.
values.tight: Keep the order; skip optional work only — second opinions, tier promotions.
values.exhausted:<vendor>: Skip that vendor's slot. Example: exhausted:openai.

budget.note: harness-route.py reads the declaration; a missing or unrecognised value is normal. SessionStart neither queries usage nor injects a BUDGET line. tight/exhausted never justify skipping required verification.

specialties.specialty: writing: design documents / operating manuals / per-language text / commit and release notes
specialties.rationale: no writing score on the leaderboards — spare

artificial_analysis.name: Artificial Analysis
artificial_analysis.provides: intelligence index; cost, latency and speed per effort
artificial_analysis.note: Per-effort index, cost and TTFT observations remain in each worker metrics record with their source and read date. Band labels are maintained independently of index rescaling.

frontierswe.name: FrontierSWE
frontierswe.provides: long-horizon agentic SWE score (Mean@5), implementation/performance/research sub-scores, average cost and duration
frontierswe.note: Collected by Epoch AI; one row per model at its top effort (max; Gemini Flash high), harness proximus. 2026-10-06: Astra 0.655, Opus 5.5 0.623, Sonnet 5.5 0.619, Fable 5.1 0.563, Gemini 3.8 Flash 0.196. No GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna or Haiku 4.5 row.
frontierswe.rationale: Measures long-horizon agentic work and lists models within weeks of release. Scores are model-level evidence at the measured effort, not per-effort values. Excluded alternatives: policy.excluded.

epoch_eci.name: Epoch Capabilities Index
epoch_eci.provides: composite capability index with confidence interval
epoch_eci.note: 2026-10-06: Opus 5.5 167.4, Astra 166.5, Sonnet 5.5 165.2, Fable 5.1 164.8, Gemini 3.8 Flash 156.9; Haiku 4.5 listed (2025). No GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Luna. A composite like the primary, so it flags disagreement rather than filling slots.

llm_stats.name: LLM Stats
llm_stats.provides: sub-scores by field, Code Arena, list prices
llm_stats.note: 2026-09-30: GPT-6.1 Sol ($2/$10 per 1M, cached input $0.10) and Opus 5.5 ($4/$20 per 1M, cached input $0.20) have 128K output. No SWE-bench or Code Arena figures populated for these rows.

livebench.name: LiveBench
livebench.provides: contamination-limited coding and agentic coding categories
livebench.note: Current tables are script-rendered and the latest public release found was 2025-04; reference only until current data can be read.

arena.name: Arena (human preference)
arena.provides: pairwise human-preference ratings, including code/webdev arenas
arena.note: Subjective preference votes; never enters scores or provisional status. Use only as a prompt for human review when it strongly contradicts the benchmark sources.

policy.rules: Fill a slot from the primary. A model listed on the secondary is evidence-backed (metrics.provisional false on all of its rows); confirm when the secondary agrees with the primary's band, and when they disagree follow the secondary for long implementations and record the cross-check in the worker note. The cross-check source only flags disagreement. Items on neither source are filled from own measurements or experience, with the evidence type marked. Reference sources never change scores.
policy.recheck_trigger: Actual model adoption, repeated task failure or observed performance change; reassess only affected bindings/policies.

last_recheck.trigger: Secondary source replacement (FrontierSWE secondary, Epoch ECI cross-check; see policy.excluded)
open: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 4.5 have no secondary row; their metrics stay provisional until FrontierSWE lists them

excluded.deepswe: Retired 2026-10-06: slow updates and newest models missing (two of eight current models listed: GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 3.8 Flash).
excluded.swe_bench_official: Verified/mini-SWE-agent rows last updated 2026-02; no current models.
excluded.epoch_swe_bench_verified: Epoch-run Verified rows stop at 2026-04 models.
excluded.scale_swe_bench_pro: Public split saturated (99.4% top) and leaderboard stalled at older models.

scale_note: Index observations use the source scale and read date recorded in metrics. Band labels are independent of leaderboard index values; an external rescale does not invalidate bindings.

selection_policy.basis: Benchmarks (capability, cost, latency, source, date) set initial bindings. Preserve measured scores and distinguish unmeasured cells.
selection_policy.objective: Sufficient task capability at efficient total completion cost/time, including handoff, verification and retries.
selection_policy.adjust_when: Repeated real-task mismatch; inspect existing run evidence and use local overrides for project-specific differences.
selection_policy.scope: Automatic assessment with volume compares USD plus declared waiting-time cost for workers and eligible direct work. Availability and trust precede the score; latency does not filter scored rows. Other paths retain measured-cost ordering with cost_tie_pct ties broken by TTFT. Bands are independent of metrics.index; S is fixed by vendor line.
selection_policy.cross_review: Host chooses the orchestrator; actual artifact authors choose eligible reviewers. Implementation shares the design author's vendor by default (vendor_precedence.implementation_default); only reviews require a different vendor. Pass all authors using --author-vendor. Reviews require explicit provenance and a fresh worker; different vendors do not guarantee correctness.

tangle: one module or screen must change
a few modules or screens must change together
many modules or screens must change together
verifier: a failing check exists or is cheap to add

assessment.mapping_note: Rows are difficulty 0/1/2; columns are exposure 0/1/2. Recent reasoning failure raises one band before the role minimum.

time_cost.note: Minutes m, tolerance T, switch s: attended costs k*(m/T)^exponent for m<=s, otherwise refocus_usd+slope_usd_per_tolerance*(m-s)/T; background/unattended cost refocus_usd+slope_usd_per_tolerance*m/T. Numeric modes retain the legacy pure-convex k*(m/T)^exponent formula. Keep refocus_usd >= k*(s/T)^exponent, otherwise the cost drops just past the switch point and a slightly slower option can look cheaper.

estimates.note: Provisional seed values from one measurement run per cell (delegate_overhead and worker values: thin-orchestration runs of 2026-10-02 with the worker advisor cost excluded, because the Claude launcher disables the advisor for workers); direct and delegate_overhead were measured with an A-band orchestrator. Volume 0 small, 1 medium, 2 large. Repeated matching DONE run records replace formula worker minutes; records are matched on model, effort and sandbox class (read-only vs write), and records without an ASSESS header count as volume-unscoped evidence. readonly_base_minutes (read-only roles: decide, plan_review, review_gate, review_deep, explore, web) seeded 2026-10-06 from this tree's DONE records: read-only median 1.9 min (n=33), write median 5.9 min (n=19). suggested_timeout_s covers worker minutes only; delegate_overhead stays in the cost score.
estimates.direct_grounded_note: Provisional seed (2026-10-06, one observation: a change scoped by a preceding review took minutes directly while the seed-based score recommended a 43-minute detached delegation). Applied to the direct usd and minutes when the router runs with --grounded; direct records carry HARNESS_GROUNDED=1 so the factor can be re-estimated from them.

AA 10-12 index / cost per task / first chunk: low 29 / $0.02 / 9.7s, medium 34 / $0.05 / 13.4s, high 38 / $0.08 / 22.7s, xhigh 41 / $0.12 / 57.1s, max 43 / $0.21 / ~290s. Pinned to low: an isolation read needs speed, not depth. Opus 5.5 low (42 / $0.55 / 7s) stays the choice when a D read needs judgment. Haiku 4.5 was 17 / $0.21 / 23.1s. S.name: Vendor top line
S.rationale: Each vendor's top-line model at medium effort (user decision 2026-10-19): design, design review and the hardest assessed judgment. Defined by vendor line, not by index. higher efforts (high/xhigh/max) stay conditional rows selected only with an explicit --worker.
